title: Annotatio V §.XI: Predicate error — Valentinian texts irrelevant to Oral-fundamentality question
pass_a_gloss: He wanders from the Predicate when he opposes to the Reformed some other sayings of Irenaeus against the Valentinians — not only nowhere adduced by me, and in no way pertaining to the matter inquired after (whether the doctrine of Oral eating is fundamental to Christian Faith), but moreover likewise most fully admitted by the Reformed: For just as the Reformed with Irenaeus affirm that the Eucharist consists of two parts.
pass_b_english: Predicate error: he aims Irenaeus’s anti-Valentinian lines at the Reformed — texts Strimesius never cited, and irrelevant to whether Oral eating is faith-fundamental.
The Reformed fully admit them anyway, and with Irenaeus say the Eucharist consists of two parts.
source_text: A Prædicato aberrat, dum Irenæi alia nonnulla, Valentinianis opposita, Reformatis opponit, non solum nullibi à me adducta, & ad rem de qua quæritur, scil. Num doctrina de Orali manducatione, Fidei Christianæ fundamentalis sit? nullo modo pertinentia, sed prætereà Reformatis itidem plenissime admissa: Quemadmodum enim Reformati cum Irenæo Eucharistiam ex duabus partibus constare ajunt.
